annotations.title: Get a copy of old mail

description: Get one copy of this mailbox's old mail: where it stands (`phase`), who acts next (`next.actor` is `owner`, `team`, `time` or `none`, and `next.reason` says on what), the step our team is running, the folder map (null until our team reads the folders), what was copied and read back, the MX record's last check (`mx.lastCheck`) and whether the copy holds the mailbox's sending (`hold`). The phases are `capture` (our team reads the folders; nothing is copied), `review` (an owner approves the map with approve_mailbox_migration_map), `prefix` (our team copies the mail that was there at the start and reads each copy back), `switch` (an owner points the mailbox's logins at the new mailbox with update_mailbox_credentials), `mx` (an owner changes the domain's MX record at their DNS provider and calls check_mailbox_migration_mx), `settle` (we wait 10 minutes for senders to see the new record), `tail` (our team copies the mail that reached the old server meanwhile) and `complete`. From the switch of logins until our team copies the last mail, nothing sends from the mailbox (`hold`): no campaign step, new message, reply or warmup, so no follow-up goes to someone whose answer is still at the old server. A copy takes up to 512 folders and messages of up to 64 MiB; one step copies up to 1000 messages and 512 MiB. Past a bound the copy stops and says why: it never skips a message. Copied mail lives in the new mailbox. The inbox in colding keeps the older mail it already shows (up to 5000 messages from the last 90 days), and the rest of the copied mail is not imported into it.
